claims.claim: Raytheon entered multi-year U.S. government frameworks in 2026 to expand production of Tomahawk, AMRAAM and Standard Missile families, with explicit annual production targets including more than 1,000 Tomahawks, at least 1,900 AMRAAMs and more than 500 SM-6s.
RTX reported delivering three times more Tomahawks in H1 2026 than H1 2025 and later received a seven-year Tomahawk contract, evidence that capacity expansion is converting into deliveries.

factors.name: defense production bottleneck
factors.basis: Long-duration frameworks and rising deliveries provide source-addressed demand and capacity signals.

risks.risk: Production expansion depends on supplier capacity, workforce, facilities and government procurement continuity.

claims.claim: RTX's explicit production targets and H1 delivery acceleration create measurable execution checkpoints rather than relying only on backlog narrative.

factors.name: capacity conversion
factors.basis: Higher delivered units plus long-duration contracts indicate tangible ramp progress.

factors.name: supply-chain burden
factors.basis: RTX itself states capacity expansion requires investment across workforce, technology, facilities and hundreds of suppliers.

risks.risk: Supplier or facility bottlenecks can prevent targeted production rates despite contracted demand.

unknowns.unknown: Scout does not infer segment margin impact or valuation from production targets.
